My research sits at the intersection of data science, ecological modeling, and climate science. I use quantitative and computational methods to understand how species respond to environmental change and to characterize spatio-temporal trends in climate.

I'm also actively expanding into new domains, applying data science to real-world problems in ecological conservation, remote sensing, renewable energy, disease ecology, epidemiology, bioinformatics, and clinical research. I enjoy working with data across disciplines, and I welcome collaborations and projects from any field where quantitative approaches can drive discovery.

## **Current Projects**

I am currently involved in two review studies:

1.  Evaluating AI methods for data cleaning and processing in large biodiversity databases – *examining how machine learning and automated pipelines can improve data quality and usability in large-scale ecological datasets*.
2.  Assessing quantitative approaches to modeling species responses to global change – *synthesizing statistical and mathematical frameworks used to predict how species respond to shifting environmental conditions*.
